# PPTX fidelity corpus

Round-trip preservation is a hard requirement (`apps/slides/CLAUDE.md`, and
`docs/adr/0002-pptx-roundtrip.md` for how): opening a deck and saving it
unchanged must produce a file PowerPoint renders identically. That claim is only
as good as the decks we test it against.

## `synthetic/`

Generated by `generate-synthetic.py` (python-pptx). Each deck isolates one
construct, so a failing round-trip points straight at what broke.

```
python3 apps/slides/tests/fixtures/pptx/generate-synthetic.py
```

| Deck | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| `empty` | the smallest thing that is still a deck |
| `placeholders` | title and body inheriting from layout and master |
| `text-formatting` | runs differing in weight, slope, size and colour in one paragraph |
| `shapes` | preset geometries with fills and lines |
| `groups-and-connectors` | nested transforms, and a connector attached to two shapes |
| `table` | a `graphicFrame` holding `a:tbl` |
| `picture` | a `p:pic` with a media part, so the rels graph is not empty |
| `notes` | a `notesSlide`, its own part with its own master |
| `many-slides` | eight slides, so ordering through `sldIdLst` is worth asserting |
| `sixteen-by-nine` | a slide size that is not the template's |

Two quirks of the generator worth knowing, because they make the fixtures
*better* rather than worse:

- `sixteen-by-nine` keeps `type="screen4x3"` on `p:sldSz` while its `cx`/`cy`
  say otherwise. PowerPoint would write `screen16x9`. A parser that reads the
  type attribute instead of the dimensions is wrong, and this catches it.
- Every deck carries eleven slide layouts whether or not a slide uses them.
  Real decks do this too, and none of them may be dropped on save.

**These are not sufficient on their own.** python-pptx writes a spare package:
one master, one theme, no `p:timing`, no effect lists, no extension lists, and a
rels graph far simpler than PowerPoint's. Passing round-trip here proves the
parser handles the constructs; it proves nothing about preserving the parts we
do not understand, which is the entire guarantee.

## `real/`

Decks actually authored by PowerPoint, exported from Google Slides, Keynote and
LibreOffice Impress. This is what preservation is judged on, and it is empty
until someone supplies files that are fine to keep in a public repository.

**Nothing personal.** The DOCX corpus was cleared of real coursework once,
history included; do not repeat that here. A deck goes in only if it would be
fine on a public website.

Wanted, at minimum:

- [ ] PowerPoint for macOS: a talk, a report, a deck from a corporate template
- [ ] PowerPoint for Windows: the same three (the ports differ in `presProps`,
      fonts and extension lists)
- [ ] Google Slides → "Download as .pptx": something with images and a table
- [ ] Keynote → "Export to PowerPoint": Keynote's export is unlike anyone else's
- [ ] LibreOffice Impress → "Save as .pptx"
- [ ] A deck with animations and transitions (must survive untouched — MVP does
      not play them, and must not lose them)
- [ ] A deck with charts, and one with SmartArt
- [ ] A deck with embedded video or audio
- [ ] A deck using a custom theme with non-default `clrScheme` and `fontScheme`
- [ ] A 100+ slide deck, for the performance budget
